title: TS SDK: ergonomic streaming shim with progress events and backpressure semantics
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: SDK consumers frequently need to move between AsyncIterable and Web Streams without losing useful semantics: explicit backpressure signals, cancellation propagation, and incremental progress events (bytes/chunks emitted). Current examples and helpers are piecemeal across the repo and don't provide a small, ergonomic surface that works consistently in Node/Browser/Deno environments.

Proposal: Add a compact TS SDK streaming shim that: (1) converts AsyncIterable<T> -> ReadableStream<T> and ReadableStream<T> -> AsyncIterable<T> without surprising buffering, (2) exposes optional progress callbacks/events (chunk count, bytes, partial tokens), (3) respects upstream abort signals and downstream backpressure by mapping desiredSize to pull frequency, (4) provides integration points for retry/resume logic (emit checkpoint tokens and allow stream to be resumed at a specific offset). The shim will be surfaced as convenience helpers on the SDK stream type: .toWebStream(opts) and .toAsyncIterable(opts).
acceptance_criteria: Helper API exists: sdkStream.toWebStream({progress?: (meta) => void, signal?: AbortSignal}) and sdkWebStream.toAsyncIterable({signal?: AbortSignal})
Cancellation: when AbortSignal is fired from consumer, upstream fetch/connection is aborted and no dangling promises remain
Backpressure: converting AsyncIterable -> ReadableStream limits internal buffering to a small bounded window; memory growth under continuous stream remains O(1) per consumer
Progress callbacks: optional progress handler receives events with chunkCount and byteEstimate for both conversions
Cross-runtime: tests pass on Node 20+, Deno, and latest Chromium/JS DOM environments (polyfill only where native ReadableStream absent)
Retry/resume hooks: stream emits checkpoint markers accessible to higher-level retry logic (unit tests exercise resume from checkpoint)
Performance: conversion overhead < 5% median latency vs baseline in microbenchmarks for typical chunk sizes (<= 64KB)
technical_notes: Implementation will use ReadableStream controller.pull() that awaits the next item from AsyncIterable; controller.desiredSize will be consulted to avoid over-pulling.
For AsyncIterable -> ReadableStream: maintain a 2-slot internal buffer; if desiredSize <= 0, pause the iteration by yielding via a Promise and resume when desiredSize > 0.
For ReadableStream -> AsyncIterable: use reader.read() loop and forward chunks to for-await-of; propagate reader.releaseLock()/cancel() on AbortSignal.
Progress events: emit lightweight events every N chunks (configurable) to avoid perf noise; event payloads are minimal: {chunkCount, approximateBytes, lastTimestamp}
Abort/teardown: wire AbortSignal so that cancel() propagates to underlying network request (fetch AbortController) and rejects pending next() promises; add finalization callback for telemetry.

Retries/resume: design checkpoint metadata (monotonic chunk index + optional byte offset) that higher-level retry middleware can serialize. Shim only surface hooks and does not perform automatic resume to keep concerns separated.

Runtime variations: Node has experimental/unstable web stream support; include a small internal polyfill path that uses stream.Readable from 'stream' when web streams not available. Keep polyfill opt-in to avoid shipping large bundles by default.
Types: expose strong TypeScript generics while keeping runtime footprint minimal. API should be trivial to tree-shake.

Trade-offs: tight backpressure mapping increases complexity and edge-case handling (e.g., sudden spikes in desiredSize). We accept a bounded internal buffer and modest microtask scheduling as a compromise for ergonomics.
implementation_timeline: Week 1: design RFC + proto implementation (AsyncIterable->ReadableStream path, basic progress events)
Week 2: complete reverse path (ReadableStream->AsyncIterable), add AbortSignal propagation and node polyfill
Week 3: tests (unit/e2e across runtimes), perf tuning, API polish and docs
Week 4: internal SDK code review, security review if needed, merge and cut release candidate
testing_plan: Unit tests for both conversion directions covering cancellation, error propagation, and progress callback semantics
E2E test with a test server emitting variable sized chunks and delays to validate backpressure behavior
Stress test: 100 concurrent consumers for 10k chunks each to validate bounded memory and no leaks
Cross-runtime CI job matrix: Node 20, latest Chromium headless, Deno stable
Benchmark microbench: measure latency overhead and memory delta vs a baseline passthrough implementation
rollout_plan: Merge behind feature flag in SDK (experimental API surface) for 1 minor release
Collect internal telemetry for 2 weeks: opt-in reports on cancel rates, checkpoint usage, and progress event volume
Gradual opt-out removal of feature flag once no major issues and docs/examples published
Announce in SDK changelog and migration guide with examples for common patterns (retries, UI progress bars)
